cards.note: Aspen trees (Populus tremuloides) can be found in lower elevation areas of interior and south-central regions of Alaska. These trees have white bark and rounded leaves.

cards.a: Argentina - Vegetation - Azorella Prolifera - Light Green
cards.note:
Azorella Prolifera is a plant that looks like "cushions". It is found throughout Patagonia. It's appearence depends on season.

You can see this plant in a distinctive light green color in these regions:

  • Southern Neuquen
  • Rio Negro on the roads Chasico-Laguna Blanca and Chasico-Ingeniero Jacobacci
  • Chubut in the area between Paso del Sapo and Gobernador Costa
  • Also Chubut on the National 40, south of Rio Mayo, as well as the provincial 55 branching east of the 40.
Beech forests are commonly found in the state of Tierra del Fuego.
The Butia yatay palm has arching, pinnate leaves and often grows at an incline with varying heights. It is most common in Corrientes and Parque Nacional El Palmar, Entre Rios.
Prosopis caldenia, known as the caldén, is a decently large deciduous tree with small leaves and sinuous branches. It is mainly found in La Pampa.

Trithrinax Campestris, or the caranday palm, not to be confused with the Caranday Wax Palm, is a rustic palm native to the Sierras de Córdoba with a broader distribution in San Luis and northern mountainous Argentina. It can be identified by its compact fan-like leaves with a trunk hidden by a coat of dead-leaves.

Coperinicia alba, also known as the Caranday Wax Palm, have short, fan-like leaves that tend to grow in low-density, single-species forests. Most common in Formosa, they can also be found in Chaco, Corrientes and northern Santa Fe.

Trichocereus atacamensis, or the cardón, is a cactus native to the high elevation mountain ranges of Catamarca, Tucumán, Salta and Jujuy. It can be identified by its candelabra-like appearance and fuzzy golden brown spines.

The Macaw Palm has small thin leaves with a visible spear shaped top. It can be found as a decorational plant all across Argentina, however in the wild it is most common in Formosa, Chaco and Misiones.
The monkey puzzle tree can be found in western Neuquen. The most specimens are seen on provincial road 23 + offroads, between Caviahue and Atreuco.
Pampas grass (Cortaderia selloana) is one of the most defining flora of the Pampas region. It is recognizable by its long bunched reeds and white fluffy flowerheads.
The Pink Trumpet Tree (Handroanthus impetiginosus) can be found in cities in northern Salta such as Orán, Tartagal and General Mosconi.

Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.

If you see them planted in single rows accompanied by hilly to mountainous, mediterranean landscape, as well as mediterranean agriculture (e.g. vineyards and olives) and vegetation (e.g. palm trees, platanus trees), you are likely in a town or city in the provinces of Mendoza and San Juan.

Red Baron is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue. It's found in

  • Western and Southern Santa Cruz
  • Northwestern Chubut
  • Southern Neuquen

Red Baron is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue.

In very dense assemblages, it can appear here:

  • Max South Santa Cruz, latitudes south of Rio Gallegos
  • The national 40 north of Las Horquetas (Santa Cruz)
  • The national 40 between Esquel and Estanzia Nueva Lubecka

cards.a: Argentina - Vegetation - Single Row Poplar - Flat
cards.note:
Poplar Trees are thin and tall decidiuous trees. They can be found all over Argentina.

If you see them planted in a single row and accompanied by a very flat landscape, you are in one of these places:

  • National 22 between Neuquen and Choele Choel (Rio Negro)
  • Trelew (Chubut)
  • Sarmiento (Chubut)

Stetsonia coryne, or the toothpick cactus, is a large tree-like cactus with many branches and spines resembling toothpicks. Its habitat includes a hotspot between Catamarca and Cordoba as well as the border area between Chaco, Salta and Formosa.
Wild sunflowers (Verbesina encelioides) are often found in Salta, Jujuy and Tucumán.
While Bottle Trees can be found throughout Queensland, they are planted everywhere in the city of Roma.
These brush plants are commonly seen in Western Australia.

Excoecaria parvifolia is an odd looking tree with almost creepy looking thin vine outgrowths as leaves. It seems to be found primarily found around the new 2025 white car coverage around the northern Queensland city of Gregory, Australia.
The Queensland fan palm or Australian fan palm, is a species endemic to northeastern Queensland, Australia (Specially around Cairns).
The sand palm is endemic to the north of the Northern Territory of Australia, from the Fitzmaurice River to Cape Arnhem and inland as far as Katherine.

Açai palms produce fruits that are popular globally. Most of these palms are found near Belem, but can be seen across the Amazon. They are distinct in the way the leaflets droop downward along with their unusually thin trunks.

Note by MB: They are very similar to the Jucara Palm (which grows in Southern Brazil). Tips for differentiation:

  • Acai Palms have more thick, robust leaves (comparatively)
  • Acai Palms like growing in bunches

This palm is commonly mistaken to be a Macaw Palm (Acrocomia Aculeata). The key difference is that the trunk of the "Paraguay Palm" is often smoother and less irregular. The crown can also give some hints although it's difficult to catch the differences

  • Macaw Palm: More open and irregular, with leaves spreading in different directions.
  • "Paraguay Palm": Denser and more compact, sometimes looking neater and rounder.

The distribution is also a bit different, as this palm usually is closer to Paraguay than the Macaw Palm which stretches further.
Babassu palms have long, robust leaves comprised of many leaflets. Trunk length can vary from short to tall. They are found throughout the Amazon, or more rarely, down the east coast.
Carnaúba palms have short but strong, fan-like leaves and a trunk that is smooth at the top and spiked at the bottom. They are common in Ceará but are also in Piauí and Rio Grande do Norte.
Coconut palm trees have long leaves, can grow very tall, and have thin trunks. They are common across the north eastern states and sometimes further west or south along the coast.

Closely related to the Açaí palm, they are really hard to distinguish apart from each other. However, the Açaí palm grows mostly in the northern flat regions of Brazil, while the Juçara grows in the mountainous south-east regions of Brazil anywhere from Espirito Santo down to Rio Grande do Sul.

Here some tips for differences:

  • The leaves of Jucara Palms are thinner
  • Jucara Palms have more space, they don't like growing close to each other.

Macaw palms, often called Paraguay palms, have thin leaves compared to other palms, and often have a visible spear shaped top. They are very common around Mato Grosso do Sul and the surrounding states, but can be seen much further out sometimes. These palms should be used with caution, and single trees are much less of an indicator than multiple trees.
Moriche palms have leaves with a rounded fan shape. They are most common in Amazonas, Acre, and Roraima, but can be found in all of the Amazonian states.

This species of plant, with long stems and many leaves growing up, are very common in Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte, and Paraíba. In the dry season, you can still make out the distinct long stems without leaves.

These distinct trees, called Paraná pines, have long horizontal branches with leaves only at the end. They grow mainly in the southern Brazilian states of Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.
Pine Trees are common in Southern Brazil, but are rarely ever found north of Belo Horizonte.

Queen palms have leaf stems that point upwards on the trunk and then "bow down" again to the ground due to gravity. They are native to South America. In Brazil, they are mainly found along the coast between Rio de Janeiro and Porto Alegre.

Outside of South America, they're also found in Florida and East Coast Queensland.
Very tall grass can be often seen in the centre of the country, most notably in the Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais states.

Eulychnia acida, commonly known as cactus ácido or copao, is a cactus species endemic to Chile, where it is primarily distributed in the semi-arid regions of the country. Its range includes: Atacama Region, Coquimbo Region,and Valparaíso Region.
Chilean rhubarb can commonly be found on Isla Grande, and on the mainland east of it. Chilean rhubarb can be recognized by its large, cabbage-like appearance.
It is endemic to a small area of central Chile between southern Coquimbo, Valparaíso, Santiago, O'Higgins, and northern Maule regions. They are highly concentrated around Viña del Mar.

Concepcion pines, scientifically named Pinus radiata, can be recognized by their puffy needles. They are most commonly found in Bio Bio, where the city of Concepcion is located, and less commonly in Ñuble and Araucania.

Monkey puzzles, scientifically named Araucaria araucana, are found in far eastern Araucania.

NOTE: Monkey puzzles can also be found on the other side of the Argentinian border.
These purple flowers, named Large-leaved Lupines, can commonly be found along Ruta 240.
Cacti are most commonly found in the North near Valledupar. Sometimes they can appear in Huila, too.
This tree is found mainly around Medellin, but it has been spotted in other random spots.
The Kapok tree can be found throughout Colombia, but is most common between the central and eastern mountain range.
This palm is found in mountainous regions of Colombia, mainly in Quindio, as the name suggests.

In Colombia you will most commonly find these trees that appear to have a knot on top of their trunk in the dark red areas. The province of Cordoba has the most gen 4 out of the others so if you see these in gen 4 consider Cordoba. (If the area is flat/semi hilly, You can find these trees in the mountains aswell everywhere)
These wide trees, usually near fences, are found in Northern regions, especially near Monteria and Sincelejo.

Forests made up entirely of Maritime pines (pinus pinaster) are found in the southwest of the country (Gironde and Landes departments). The whole area will be fairly flat, which is not typical of other areas with such pines.

The vegetation near the South-East coast looks very Mediterranean.

Note by MB: This is more of a vibe thing tbh.
Stone pines are commonly found along the southern coast, often planted alongside urban roads. You may however find them as north as Nantes.
Baltic Pines or Pinus sylvestris are generally more concentrated in the northeast of Germany. They can be recognized by their orange-tinged trunk.

Agaves are mostly found in Karnataka

Note by MB: This is generally a fake meta, Agaves can be found in many different places throughout India. But if you have really nothing else to go off, Karnataka is definitely a place to conside.r

Areca Palms can be recognised by their very thin trunk and a small crown.

They are most common in Assam, but also in other northeastern areas, stretiching to coastal Odisha. A second common region is Kerala and coastal Karnataka
In Assam, these white flowers can often be seen along the road in three areas: - The border to West Bengal - The border to Eastern Bhutan - West of Nagaon.

Recognition (most visible when you look at the bottom of the crown):

  • symmetrical pattern of needles on twigs
  • thin twigs
  • twigs draping down

Found in:

  • mostly Western Sikkim and Sangti, Manda La, Salari (Arunachal Pradesh)
  • often in Khellong, Rupa (Arunachal Pradesh)
  • sometimes Rest of Sikkim, and Arunachal, west of Jamiri
  • rarely in West Bengal near Sikkim Border.

Recognition:

  • whiteish-greyish tinge
  • Short needles
  • long slender cones
  • two rows of hanging needles
  • many branches, little space between them

Found in:

  • Max West Arunachal, Mechuka
  • sometimes Ziro, Neora Valley National Park (West Bengal)
  • very rarely Sikkim

Recognition:

  • individual branches well visible
  • edges of branches have thin brush of new needles
  • in higher elevation, the crown will be conical
  • needles drape down in all directions

Found in:

  • mostly: Max West Arunachal; Road south of Harsil
  • sometimes: Dharamshala, Manali, Kullu, Shimla, Sarahan, Southern Uttarakhand Mountains
  • rarely: Further inside the Uttarakhand mountains
Calotropis Procera is found all over Rajasthan and less in surrounding states so it is a good clue for Rajasthan if you have a lot of it.

Recognition

  • round crown
  • young pines: conical crown, thick brush for new needles Found in
  • Mountainous Uttarakhand; Shimla, Dalhousie (Himachal Pradesh); Elevated Jammu / Kashmir
  • Sometimes Dharamshala (Himachal Pradesh)
  • Rarely low elevation dry valleys in Western Arunachal Pradesh

Coconut palms are most common in Kerala, the Western Half of Karnataka and Southern Coastal Maharashtra In general, they appear near Coasts, near the border to Bangladesh, and anywhere South of Central Telangana

cards.a: India - Vegetation - Combination of Date Palm & Palmyra Palm
cards.note: In Jharkhand, you will very often see the combination of date palms (a lot of them) and palmyra palms. I think it is one of the best clues for getting Jharkhand because it’s pretty unique. I also saw a lot of that combination of palms in Telangana so be careful and look for text before guessing.
Date palms can be found in Central India. They appear North of the Latitude of Chhattisgarh, except for Himalayan states, the Northeast and Western Gujarat/RJ.

cards.a: India - Vegetation - Date Palm - Tamil Nadu
cards.note: Within Tamil Nadu, date palms can be found in the North-East.
These 'dead'-looking trees are a very strong point to go to Rajasthan. They are concentrated mostly southwest of Sikar.
Doum palms, which appear similar to Palmyra palms but with multiple branches, are almost exclusive to the union territory of Diu.
Eucalyptus trees are a good clue for the Uttarakhand foothills and nearby areas in Uttar Pradesh.
This type of cacti (Euphorbia neriifolia) can commonly be seen as part of fences throughout Gujarat, western Maharashtra and the southern half of Rajasthan.
South of Udaipur, you can find a very distinct landscape with narrow hills and a lot of this type of cactus (Euphorbia).

Recognition:

  • downward bending branches
  • very short needles

Found in

  • Shimla, Dalhousie, Dharamshala, Palampur, Kasol, Jibhi, South of Kullu, South of Manali (HP); Road from Harsil to Gangotri (UK) and Southwestern UK in general
  • sometimes in Kangra, Solan, Manali-Dalang road (HP) and around Rudrapayag (UK)
  • rarely in eastern Uttarakhand

Recognition:

  • twig with two symmetrical rows of short needles
  • downward bending twigs
  • crowns look a bit disorganized

Found in:

  • South of Senge and South of Dirang (Western Arunachal Pradesh)
The endangered Indian pitcher plant is exclusive to the Khasi Hills, which are mainly in Meghalaya. They can occasionally be spotted on road sides, especially on the NH206 north of Umlārem.

This tree, often called Jand by Indians, can be recognized by the clusters of leaves at the end of thick branches.

It is found in Northern Rajasthan and Southern Haryana/Punjab.

Recognition:

  • puffy, conical crown
  • smooth reddish bark with parallel vertical indents
  • "sea grass twigs" (look at picture #3)
  • twigs growing in all directions

Found in:

  • Sikkim/WB Border
  • Meghalaya Hills
  • Dirang, Khellong, Bomdila (Arunachal)
  • sometimes more north in Sikkim and west of Jamiri (Arunachal)
  • rarely east of Jamiri (AR)

Recognition:

  • disorganized crowns, neither conical nor round
  • younger pines can appear round, but have shorter needles

Found in:

  • Meghalaya Hills
  • Raga & South of Ziro Junction (Arunachal Pradesh)
  • Imphal (Manipur)
  • Champhai, Darlawn (Mizoram) Less commonly:
  • Road from Ziro to Raga
  • North Vanlaiphai (Mizoram) Rarely:
  • Rest of Meghalaya and Mizoram
  • Arunachal Pradesh / Nagaland border

Parasol leaf tree (Macaranga peltata) is common along the southwestern coast anywhere south of Mumbai and seems to be virtually exclusive to that area, I have yet to find it anywhere else in India. To identify it, look for the teardrop shape of the leaves and the spot where the leaf stem connects to the inner part of the leaf blade.

Recognition:

  • Dense Foliage
  • Shoots drape downwards

Found in:

  • Shimla, Kullu, Manali (Himachal Pradesh)
  • Uttarkashi, Dehradun, Ukhimath (Uttarakhand)
  • to a lesser extent: general area between Dehradun and Ukhimath
  • rarely in Eastern Uttarakhand

Palmyra Palms have a round crown with fan shaped leaves and a trunk with consistent thickness, giving them a lollipop shape.

They appear mostly in 3 areas:

  • Central Bihar
  • Coastal Pondicherry towards Andhra Pradesh/Odisha border + Telangana
  • Around Mumbai

They are also common in

  • coastal states from Tamil Nadu to West Bengal
  • Bihar & Eastern UP
  • Telangana
  • Eastern Gujarat

Recognition:

  • Symmetrical Branches
  • Layered Clusters
  • Clusters shaped like an "inverse function" (see images)
  • narrow, conical, dense foliage

Found in:

  • Jibhi (HP), Chinyalisour, Ukhimath (UK)
  • sometimes Shimla (HP), Range from Dehradun to Rishikesh (UK)
  • rarely remaining UK Mountains; Dharamshala, Palampur, Kullu, Kasol, Manali (HP)
Found in Gujarat, mainly at the southern peninsula (could be fake)
West of Mount Abu, you can find a lot of Euphorbia cacti with flat landscape. Note that this meta is only specific for Rajasthan, Euphorbia appears in other states, like Gujarat, too.

Recognition:

  • Symmetrical Shoots
  • Longer Needles
  • Small shoots make triangular shape
  • Seperated clusteres at different hights

Found in

  • Senge, Manda La (AR)

Recognition:

  • no needles in winter (which is currently all coverage in India with this tree)
  • Conical structure that resembles a christmas tree
  • lighter needles (if present)

Found in:

  • around Senge
  • sometimes around Manda La (both Arunachal Pradesh)

Recognition:

  • needles organized in seperated clumps
  • darker than pines
  • individual branches visible (on high trees)
  • new shoots & many buds often visible from afar
  • Unique branch structure

Extremely rare in India, so far only a singular tree has been found in Manda La.
Teak forests in wet season with boxy car can be found around the Gujarat-Maharashtra border between Surat and Nashik. The trees are quite distinctive, tall and narrow.
If you see a Coconut, hedge in the south eastern half towards Andhra Pradesh, it has more of them.
Areca palms (Areca catechu) are most prominent in western Sumatra; however they can also be seen elsewhere less commonly. They can be recognised by their relatively short and thick leaves.

Coastal she-oak (Casuarina equisetifolia) can be found along the coast throughout much of the country, but particularly in Sumatra, Kalimantan and Java. Their leaves resemble the needles of pine trees, but are noticeably longer. Another species of she-oak can be found in mountainous regions throughout the country.

Coconut palms (Cocos nucifera) can be found in many regions throughout Indonesia, but are most abundant along the coast, especially in western Sumatra, southern Java, northern Sulawesi and North Maluku.

Footstool palm (Saribus rotundifolius) has fan-shaped leaves similar to those of Palmyra palm; however the crown is more open, the leaves are thinner and the palm itself is usually taller. It can be found most notably in Sulawesi and more rarely in other parts of the country.

Gebang palm (Corypha utan) can at first glance look similar to both Palmyra and footstool palm due to its fan-shaped leaves, however the leaves are noticeably larger, stiffer and more upright in contrast to the round crown shape of both Palmyra and footstool palm. Unlike most palms, the gebang palm will only flower once at the end of its life in a dramatic gesture where the leaves wither away and it shoots one large inflorescence into the heavens before it dies. It is found mainly in the east of the country, namely Sulawesi and the Nusas.
Giant milkweed (Calotropis gigantea) is a small shrub with thick round leaves and pale flowers. It can be found in dry regions of Indonesia, namely the Nusas and parts of Java and Sulawesi.

Palmyra palms (Borassus flabellifer) can be recognised by their fan-shaped leaves and dense round crowns. Compared to footstool palm, the crown is more dense, the leaves are heavier and the palm itself is usually shorter. It is found in dry parts of the country, namely the Nusas and South Sulawesi.

Sumatran pines (Pinus merkusii) in Indonesia can be found in a few pockets across the country, notable areas include North Sumatra and Java. They can be recognised by having long needles for leaves, but be careful not to confuse them with she-oak, which has even longer leaves.

White leadtree (Leucaena leucocephala) can be recognised by its delicate featherlike (bipinnate) leaves. Fruits are often also visible in the form of legume pods. It can be found mainly in the Nusas as well as a few other dry areas of the country.

In general, bamboo grows more often in the south, and slowly decreases further north. Population size and areas where it grows can vary, so use this information primarily in helping assist your region guess.

Chinese Silver Grass, referred to as Kyushu grass, is indeed very abundant on the island of Kyushu. However, use this tip with caution, as they can be seen outside of this area.

NOTE: Another notable region they can be found in is the prefectures of Niigata, Yamagata and Akita. Though, combining the rather large quantity found on Kyushu, its normally distinct vegetation, along with other information, there often will be a clear distinction.

Giant butterbur (commonly referred to as cabbage) is abundant in Hokkaido and some northern prefectures. Plants found south of Hokkaido often have smaller leaves. It is often found growing along the roadside.

Japanese White Birch grows dominantly in the Chubu and Hokkaido regions, and to a lesser extent in Tohoku. Small areas of white birch can be found throughout Japan, so use this information primarily to help assist your region guess.

NOTE: Japanese Beech is another species of tree found in Japan. They, however, have more grey and spotted bark, as opposed to the mostly white Japanese White Birch.
If you see a cactus in a coastal area, you're probably in Oaxaca.

blue, but less blue than tequilana, smaller grouping

found in Central Oaxaca

The rough century plant looks similar to the pulque agave but its leaves are blueish and it is much smaller. It is distributed nearly identically to A. lechuguilla (Durango and Coahuila, especially around Saltillo and West of Torreon, rarely SLP and Hidalgo), and is often difficult to spot from the road, only barely visible in the distance in batches.

Agave cupreata is a very rarely observed agave that is localised to central Guerrero. Its name is apt - it has a much more pronounced, cup-like appearance than other agaves, with the leaves lurching inwards. It is often found growing on walls in groups as depicted.

A. karwinskii is exclusively seen in the central desert region of Oaxaca, mostly near the town Miahuatlán de Porfirio Díaz, even though technically its native distribution extends elsewhere in the state and barely into Puebla. Its spiky thin leaves, protruding from the centre in a cylindrical formation, make it quite distinct from other common agaves.

Agave lechuguilla is a very frequent sighting in the hills of Durango and Coahuila, particularly around the cities of Saltillo and west of Torreon. More rarely it can be found in San Luis Potosi and Hidalgo. It is distinguished by its slick, lime-green leaves that almost look as if they are combed to one side.

Myrtillocactus Geometrizans is a species of cactus in the genus Myrtillocactus, native to central and northern Mexico. It is especially abundant in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo, and much more rarely Guanajuato.
Boojum trees can be recognized by their alien, tentacle-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.
Brittlebush are small shrubs with bright silver-grey leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.
Pachycereus weberi is widespread in the Mexican states of Puebla, Guerrero, Morelos, Hidalgo and Oaxaca at altitudes of 600 to 1,500 m.

This tall, columnar cactus, with no branches, is native to northern Oaxaca and southern Puebla, and another of the many species present there. Much less commonly but still possibly it can be seen in central Guerrero.
The species originates from Mexico (Guerrero, Michoacán, Oaxaca, southern Puebla). It will almost always place you somewhere in Oaxaca, usually central in the state.
Coconut palms can be found all across the coast, but are often found in large groups in Guerrero and Colima.

This palm is recognizable through its round fan leaves.

Within Mexico, it's usually found in Yucatan.
The golden glow of the fruit cholla is also unmistakable, and present mostly in the Western Half of Sonora.

Pachycereus pringlei is a species of large cactus native to northwestern Mexico, in the states of Baja California, Baja California Sur. It can rarely be found on the Sonoran coast, around the area south of Puerto Libertad on the 3.
These gold tufts of grass in a line right next to the road are most commonly found in Coahuila.

The Indian Comb (Pachycereus pecten-aboriginum), is a common cactus that always implies Sinaloa, or south Sonora near Sinaloa, although technically its habitat extends elsewhere. Its densely packed branches emerge from a single stem, but most recognisable is its inflorescence - the brightly coloured flowers which usually adorn the tip of its arms.
This species is found mostly in Mexico, mainly in Sonora and southern Baja California and Northern Sinaloa. If the cactus is significantly larger than 3m, it's probably in Southern Baja.
A huge abundance of Organ Pipe Cacti it is usually indicative of the reserve El Cajón del Diablo, south of Hermosillo.

In Pitaya the branches less organically sprout from the ground in the weed-like manner of the Organ Pipe, and instead curl smoothly outwards from a central stem.

It is mostly found in Jalisco, south of Guadalajara. Less commonly, it's seen in Guanajuato. It can be seen in Queretaro too, but surprisingly rarely.

Prickly pear cacti with a total absence of other cacti, yucca, agaves or in general succulent plants except for the prickly pear is generally a good signal for the centre-west (Jalisco, Guanajuato, Michoacan).

Prickly pear cacti are distinct with their flat oval-shaped pads. They are noticeably more common centrally and are rarely seen in southern and coastal states.

They are also good for some 50/50:

  • Durango > Chihuahua
  • Durango > Sonora (less reliable)
  • Nuevo Leon > Tamaulipas
  • Other States > Mexico State

Agave salmiana, colloquially the pulque agave, is native to central Mexico. Agaves in general are distinguishable by their crown-like appearance, with stiff leaves which fan outwards symmetrically. The pulque agave is no different, but has green leaves, relatively smooth edges, and flat leaves that curl slightly away from the central axis.

Note its distribution, in an arc around Mexico City and a second pocket of endemism which straddles San Luis Potosi city and Aguascalientes.
These thin, white-barked trees can be found in the Yucatan peninsula, but are most prevalent in Quintana Roo.

This palm seems to be prominent in coastal Texas, the east and the south coast of Mexico, Yucatán peninsula, and Guatemala. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.

Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed.

Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.

Sabal Rosei is native to the Pacific coast of Mexico, from Sinaloa to Jalisco but mostly concentrated in the state of Nayarit. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.

Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.

Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed.

This palm grows pretty much exclusively in the Yucatán peninsula. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.

Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips.

Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.

The Saguaro is endemic to the Sonoran Desert and is found primarily in western Sonora in Mexico, and in western Arizona in the US. Elevation is a limiting factor to its environment, as the saguaro is sensitive to extended frost or cold temperatures.
A rare and tall cactus, the thin and twirling branches of S. fricii are unique to Michoacan, especially on the 37D, where it is abundantly spammed.
These clumps of grass in almost a teardrop shape are common in the region around Tlaxcala.

The tree cholla is a cactus, and its skeletal, discoloured arms spurting in every direction make it recognisable.

Mostly found in San Luis Potosi, Queretaro and Hidalgo, often in Coahuila and Durango and rarely in Zacatecas.
If it is present in groups, Tree Cholla is usually a good indication of San Luis Potosi.
It is native to central mexico, most commonly found in Zacatecas and San Luis Potosí although it can be seen anywhere from Nuevo León down to Puebla, in dry regions.
The Attalea rostrata is a huge palm recognizable from its upright leaves, almost resembling an umbrella. It is mostly exclusive to Veracruz and Tabasco, and can be rarely found in Chiapas.
Oaxaca is very diverse in Cacti, so if you see a strange cactus, or one that isn't explained in this map, you can consider going Oaxaca.

This species of fern (Pteridium aquilinum, also known as bracken) which typically has a fairly tall stem and many wide leafs branching out, is mostly found in the south of Norway. Beware that other species of ferns can be found further north.
Brightly colored moss is common to find in the area between Lillehammer and Oppdal
Maples are mainly found in the south, particularly by the farmlands around Oslo.
Oaks are mainly found in the far south of Norway.
Pines are most common in coastal and far inland areas in the southern half of the country.
Spruces are mainly found in the southern half of the country, particularly in the southeast and around Trondheim.

Coconut palms (and other species of tall palms) can sometimes be seen in coastal areas of Peru, mainly north of Lima. They are mainly found in the agricultural areas which are typically found around the major coastal cities.

Pine plantations are typically found in higher elevation areas of the country, away from the coastal deserts and Amazonian Regions. The most common types of pine trees planted are Pinus radiata and Pinus patula.

Moluccan albizia are trees with light coloured trunks and pinnate leaves near the top of the tree. They are mainly found on Mindanao and are especially common in the eastern and central regions of the island.

Uniquely tall Cook pine trees are found mostly between the cities of East London and Durban along the southeastern coast.

NOTE: These are planted and not native, so they can be found anywhere along the coast.

Turkish pines (pinus brutia) are mainly found near the Mediterranean coast.

NOTE: Turkish pines can appear very similar to Aleppo pines, which are uncommon in Turkey, but are often found in other Mediterranean countries.

The Balsam Fir is a very symmetric tree. It has pretty dark needles and often grows close to the ground.

Within the US, you will find it in the Northeast, starting in Northern New York. You can also see it near the Great Lakes, on Latitudes similar to Vermont/Maine.

You may already know Ohio’s nickname, the Buckeye State, but despite the name, buckeyes grow in other states too. They’re most commonly seen in the east from Ohio down through West Virginia, Virginia, and Kentucky to Tennessee and North Carolina. Some can be found in Missouri too.

California is the only state in the west where you can see buckeyes.
Sabal palmetto is native to the subtropical coastal regions of the American states of Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, southeastern North Carolina, and extreme southern Texas.

cards.a: United States - Vegetation - California Fan Palm
cards.note: Washingtonia filifera is the only palm native to the Western United States and one of the country's largest native palms.

Grass that is used in lawns in the southern US (colloquially known as Bermuda and St. Augustine grasses) go dormant in the winter months. This causes the lawns to turn beige or light brown in winter; whereas grasses used in more northern areas of the US stay much greener in winter.

Extremely tall conifer trees (Douglas firs) with a dark brown bark, and dark green leaves, can most commonly be seen in Cascadia. Notably, they can also be found in northern California, Idaho and as far east as Montana.

Beware that they are also commonly found in British Columbia.

cards.a: United States - Vegetation - Gumbo Limbo Tree
cards.note: The Gumbo Limbo tree can be recognized by its red bark and by its irregular, sometimes twisting trunks. Its leaves are green and oval shaved. You will only find it in Coastal Florida, south of Orlando and south of Tampa.

Palm trees are common in coastal areas of the Southeastern states, as well as the Desert Southwest region. Shown here is the Mexican Fan Palm, which is most common in California and along the Gulf Coast, but other palm tree types have a similar range.

Aspen trees are thin trees with white barks that often grow in groups. In the contiguous states, you can find it in North-East USA, all states that border the great lakes (+NE-Iowa), in Northern Idaho and in random areas in the West.
Great Basin Sagebrush (Artemisia tridentata) is a short, shrubby blue-green bush that is common in the interior western United States.It is most common in arid areas.
Saguaro cacti are most commonly shaped like tall, straight tubes with several branches extending from the main tube. They are most commonly found in southern Arizona, on the Sonoran border.
Saw Palmetto grows in clumps or dense thickets in sandy coastal areas, and as undergrowth in pine woods or hardwood hammocks. You can find it in coastal areas of Florida and Georgia.

cards.a: United States - Vegetation - Southern Live Oak
cards.note: This tree can commonly be found in Florida and along the southern coast as shown by the range map. A southern live oak will often have Spanish moss hanging from the branches, giving the tree a pendulous appearance.
This tree can only be found in the South. However, southern magnolias don’t grow in southern Florida. The range stretches from Orlando and Tampa to North Carolina and Texas.

The loblolly pine (Pinus taeda), and longleaf pine (Pinus palustris), commonly referred to as southern pines in the community, are found throughout the southeastern US. They are a great way to recognize this region, as they are abundant, recognizable and mostly limited to this part of the country. They tend to be tall, with fluffy-looking clusters of pine needles.
Spanish moss, appearing as greyish white drapes, can sometimes be seen on trees in the deep south.
Acacia trees, recognisable by their relatively short height and umbrella-like flat crowns, are most abundant and common in northern Oman, but can also be found close to the rest of the coast.
Coconut palms are usually found near Salalah.
Date palm plantations are most common along the northern coast.
